data_description.pairing_instructions_generic:
1. Put your bed in pairing mode (hold lamp button until blue light blinks, or unplug for 30+ seconds)
2. Click 'Pair Now'
data_description.pairing_instructions_okin:
1. Put the OKIN base into Bluetooth pairing mode by power-cycling the control box: unplug it for ~30 seconds, then plug it back in. The status light blinks blue, then turns green after ~20 seconds. (Some models instead use the under-bed lamp/light button - hold it until the light blinks blue.) There is no separate Bluetooth pairing button; any Pair/Learn button on the box only syncs the RF remote.
2. While the light is active, click 'Pair Now'.
data_description.pairing_instructions_sleep_number:
1. Put your bed in pairing mode (hold the side pairing button until the blue light blinks)
2. Click 'Pair Now'
data_description.pairing_instructions_leggett_gen2:
1. Unplug your bed's power cord and remove any batteries from the power supply.
2. Plug the bed back in. Wait for a small chime and a pulsing blue light under the bed.
3. While the light is pulsing, promptly click 'Pair Now'.
data_description.bond_state: What this Home Assistant host already knows about a bond for this bed.
data_description.bond_state_proxy: ℹ️ This bed will pair through a Bluetooth proxy, which keeps the bond itself. Home Assistant cannot read or remove a bond stored on a proxy, so it cannot tell you whether one already exists.
data_description.bond_state_unreadable: ℹ️ Home Assistant could not read the Bluetooth bonds on this host, so it cannot tell whether this bed is already paired.
data_description.bond_state_existing: ✅ This Home Assistant host already has a Bluetooth bond for this bed. The actions below reflect whether the selected adapter can use it and whether it can be replaced safely.
data_description.bond_state_multiple: ⚠️ More than one Bluetooth adapter on this host is bonded to this bed. Pairing again will use whichever adapter Home Assistant connects through.
data_description.bond_state_none: ℹ️ This Home Assistant host has no Bluetooth bond for this bed yet.
data_description.bond_state_route_uncertain: ℹ️ This Home Assistant host has a Bluetooth bond for this bed, but more than one adapter or proxy could take the connection, and Home Assistant chooses which when it connects. Setting up with the existing bond would assume a route it cannot guarantee, so pair again instead and let the connection record which transport really owns the bond.
data_description.bond_state_mismatched: ℹ️ This Home Assistant host has a Bluetooth bond for this bed, but on a different adapter from the one this connection will use. Bonds belong to one adapter, so that one cannot be used here. Pair again to create a bond on this adapter, or select the bonded adapter instead.

data_description.bond_state: What this Home Assistant host already knows about a bond for this bed.

data_description.action: Try again keeps the bed type, adapter and protocol settings you already chose.
data_description.outcome_no_run: ❌ Pairing did not run. Select **Try again**.
data_description.outcome_verified_local: ✅ Paired, and the bond was confirmed. It is stored on this Home Assistant host ({transport}).
data_description.outcome_verified_proxy: ✅ Paired, and the bond was confirmed. It is stored on the Bluetooth proxy {transport}, not on Home Assistant, so moving this bed to a different proxy will mean pairing again.
data_description.outcome_verified_unknown: ✅ Paired, and the bond was confirmed. Home Assistant could not tell which adapter or proxy carried it, so it does not know where the bond is stored.
data_description.outcome_existing_verified_local: ✅ The existing bond works. It is stored on this Home Assistant host ({transport}), and setup will use it as it is.
data_description.outcome_existing_verified_proxy: ✅ The existing bond works. It is stored on the Bluetooth proxy {transport}, so moving this bed to a different proxy will mean pairing again.
data_description.outcome_existing_verified_unknown: ✅ The existing bond works, but Home Assistant could not tell which adapter or proxy carried the check, so it does not know where the bond is stored.
data_description.outcome_unproven: ⚠️ Pairing completed, but this bed gives Home Assistant no way to confirm the bond. Setup will finish and record that pairing happened, so the first connection does not try to pair on top of it. If the bond did not really form, Home Assistant will raise a repair asking you to pair again.
data_description.outcome_not_advertising: ❌ The bed is not advertising, so no connection was attempted. Put it into pairing mode or move it closer to an adapter or proxy, then select **Try again**.
data_description.outcome_auth_failed: ❌ The bed connected, but the link is still unauthenticated, so the bond did not form. Put the bed back into pairing mode and select **Try again**.
data_description.outcome_inconclusive: ⚠️ Home Assistant could not confirm the existing bond either way: the check timed out or the bed does not answer it. The bond may well be fine. You can try again, or pair from scratch if the bed does not respond afterwards.
data_description.outcome_unsupported: ❌ This Bluetooth adapter or proxy cannot pair. ESPHome proxies need ESPHome 2024.3.0 or newer; otherwise pair through a Bluetooth adapter on the Home Assistant host.
data_description.outcome_removal_failed: ❌ The existing bond could not be removed, so pairing was not attempted and the old bond is still in place. Try again, and use Remove the Bluetooth bond from the device's options if it persists.
data_description.outcome_in_use: ❌ The bed's Bluetooth connection is already in use. Beds allow only one connection at a time, so close the manufacturer's app and put the physical remote down, then select **Try again**.
data_description.outcome_no_slots: ❌ Every Bluetooth adapter and proxy that can reach this bed is out of free connections. Free one up, or add another proxy, then select **Try again**.
data_description.outcome_timed_out: ❌ The bed stopped responding partway through. Put it back into pairing mode and select **Try again**.
data_description.outcome_connection_failed: ❌ Could not pair. Another app or the bed's own remote may be holding the bed's connection, or it may be out of range. Select **Try again**.
data_description.outcome_removal_unconfirmed: ⚠️ Home Assistant could not confirm what happened to the existing bond, so pairing was not attempted and the bond may still be in place. Check the host's Bluetooth settings, then select **Try again**.

pairing_replace_confirm.title: Replace the existing bond
pairing_replace_confirm.description:
**{name}** already has a Bluetooth bond with this Home Assistant host, stored on **{transport}**.

Continuing removes that bond and pairs again from scratch. Home Assistant checks first that the bed is actually reachable, so a sleeping bed will not be left without a bond.

Select **Submit** to replace it, or go back to keep it and use it as it is.

pair_beds.title: Combine two beds
pair_beds.description: Combine two existing beds into one paired device with Left, Right and combined controls. The two original beds are removed; their entity history follows. Pairing is for sides that move independently — if a sync cable already keeps both sides together, keep a single bed instead.

remove_bond.title: Remove the Bluetooth bond
remove_bond.description:
This removes the Bluetooth bond that **{name}** ({address}) has with this Home Assistant host.

**Bond stored on:** {transport}{provenance}

Home Assistant will disconnect from the bed first. Afterwards the bed will need pairing again before it can be controlled, and you may need to put it back into pairing mode to do that.

This does **not** delete the Adjustable Bed device or its settings. Select **Submit** to remove the bond, or go back to leave it alone.

data_description.outcome_removed: ✅ The Bluetooth bond was removed and the removal was confirmed.

remove_bond_side.title: Choose a bed side
remove_bond_side.description: A combined bed has a separate Bluetooth bond for each physical side. Choose the side whose bond you want to remove.

unpair.title: Split paired bed
unpair.description: Restore the Left and Right sides as separate Adjustable Bed entries. Side entities keep their entity IDs, history, names, and areas. Combined controls are removed.

pair_sides.title: Enable paired-side controls
pair_sides.description: Expose Left, Right, and Both controls for this bed while keeping its existing Bluetooth address and config entry. This is reversible. Existing standalone behavior is restored if you revert it later.

revert_sides.title: Restore standalone controls
revert_sides.description: Remove the Left, Right, and Both surface and restore this config entry exactly as it was before paired-side controls were enabled. Existing standalone entity IDs and history are preserved.

abort.remove_bond_proxy_owned: **{name}** is paired through a Bluetooth proxy ({transport}), not through this Home Assistant host, so Home Assistant cannot remove that bond. The bond lives on the proxy itself: clear it there (an ESPHome proxy forgets its bonds when it is reflashed or factory reset), or set the bed's preferred adapter to a Bluetooth adapter on this host and pair again.
abort.remove_bond_no_bond: This Home Assistant host has no Bluetooth bond stored for **{name}** ({address}), so there is nothing to remove.
abort.remove_bond_bluez_unavailable: Home Assistant could not read the Bluetooth bonds on this host, so it will not try to remove one. This usually means it has no local Bluetooth adapter, or no access to the system D-Bus.
abort.remove_bond_ambiguous: Home Assistant cannot tell which Bluetooth bond you mean for **{name}** ({address}). Either more than one adapter on this host is bonded to it, or the adapter it was paired through no longer holds a bond. Set the bed's preferred adapter to the one you want to clear, then try again.
abort.remove_bond_changed: The Bluetooth bonds on this host changed while the confirmation was open, so nothing was removed. Open **Remove the Bluetooth bond** again to see the current state and confirm from there.

confirm.title: Pair your adjustable bed
confirm.description:
**{name}** ({address}) requires a Bluetooth bond before it can be controlled.

1. Put the bed into pairing mode. **OKIN bases** (Okimat, Okin CST, Nectar OKIN-*, Mattress Firm 900-O): power-cycle the control box — unplug it for ~30 seconds, then plug it back in (the light blinks blue, then turns green); they have no Bluetooth pairing button. **Leggett & Platt Smart Bed (LP Comfort Connect)**: unplug the bed's power cord, remove any batteries from the power supply, then plug it back in — wait for a chime and a pulsing blue light under the bed. **Other beds**: hold the pairing button on the control box or remote until its light blinks.
2. While the bed is in pairing mode, promptly press **Submit** to pair.

Pairing happens on your Home Assistant host or Bluetooth proxy — not your phone. ESPHome proxies must run ESPHome 2024.3.0 or newer.

If pairing keeps failing and the log names `AuthenticationFailed` or `AuthenticationRejected`, the bond is failing at the authentication stage rather than timing out, and retrying unchanged rarely helps. One common cause is stored pairing keys that no longer match: the bed still stores a pairing for the adapter you are connecting from, while that adapter no longer has the matching key. Clearing only one side does not help in that case.

Remove the stored pairing on the adapter that connects to the bed: on a Home Assistant host that is `bluetoothctl remove {address}`; if you connect through an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy the bond is stored on the proxy and has to be cleared there. Then clear the bed's own stored pairings the way its manufacturer documents, and pair again.

proxy_bond.title: The bond is stored on a Bluetooth proxy
proxy_bond.description:
**{name}** ({address}) last failed to authenticate through **{transport}**, which is a Bluetooth proxy rather than this Home Assistant host.

A proxy keeps its own Bluetooth bonds, and Home Assistant can neither read nor remove them, so there is nothing this repair can safely change.

To clear it: reflash or factory reset the proxy, which makes it forget its bonds, then put the bed into pairing mode so it bonds again. Alternatively set this bed's preferred adapter to a Bluetooth adapter on the Home Assistant host and pair there, where the bond can be managed.

stale_bond_confirm.title: Replace a bond the bed no longer accepts
stale_bond_confirm.description:
**{name}** ({address}) connects, but every encrypted read is refused. That is what happens when this host still holds a Bluetooth bond the bed itself has forgotten, usually after the bed was reset or paired with something else.

**Bond stored on:** {transport}

Continuing removes that bond and creates a new one. Home Assistant checks the bed is reachable before removing anything, so a sleeping bed will not be left without a bond, and the new bond is only recorded once it has been confirmed to work.

Put the bed into pairing mode, then select **Submit**.

abort.pairing_failed: Pairing didn't complete. Put the bed back into pairing mode (OKIN bases: unplug the control box ~30s, then plug it back in; Leggett & Platt Smart Bed: unplug the bed and remove the power-supply batteries, then plug it back in and wait for the chime and pulsing blue light; other beds: hold the pairing button), make sure it is in range of your Home Assistant adapter or an ESPHome proxy on 2024.3.0+, then run this repair again. If the log names `AuthenticationFailed` or `AuthenticationRejected`, the bond failed to authenticate. If it keeps happening, clear the stored pairing both on the adapter you connect from and on the bed itself, then try again.
abort.proxy_bond_guidance: Nothing was changed. The Bluetooth bond for this bed is stored on a proxy, where Home Assistant cannot reach it.
abort.stale_bond_recovery_failed: The bond could not be recovered, so this repair stays open. Put the bed into pairing mode and run it again.
abort.recovery_success: ✅ The Bluetooth bond was confirmed. The bed should respond normally now.
abort.recovery_not_advertising: ❌ The bed is not advertising, so nothing was changed and the old bond is still in place. Put the bed into pairing mode and run this repair again.
abort.recovery_unpair_failed: ❌ The old bond could not be removed, so nothing else was attempted.
abort.recovery_unpair_unconfirmed: ❌ Removing the old bond could not be confirmed, so it may or may not still be there and no new one was made. Put the bed into pairing mode and run this repair again.
abort.recovery_failed_unchanged: ❌ The existing bond could not be checked safely, so nothing was changed. Make sure the bed is in range and run this repair again.
abort.recovery_partial: ❌ The old bond was removed but the new one could not be confirmed, so this repair stays open. Put the bed into pairing mode and run it again.

combine_two_beds.title: Combine two beds into one (Dual Bed)

init.title: Could any two be sides of one bed?
init.description:
Home Assistant found {count} standalone beds: {names}.

If any two entries control the independent sides of one physical bed, choose them as Left and Right. If none share a physical bed, mark the displayed beds as separate and this suggestion will not return while only those beds remain.

pair_beds.title: Combine two beds
pair_beds.description: Combine two existing beds into one paired device with Left, Right and combined controls. The two original beds are removed; their entity history follows. Pairing is for sides that move independently: if a sync cable already keeps both sides together, keep a single bed instead.

error.unknown: The selected bed is no longer available. Reload Repairs and try again.
error.same_device: Pick two different beds; you selected the same one for both sides.
error.same_address: Both selections point at the same Bluetooth address. Pick two different beds.
error.mismatched_bed_types: Those two beds use different protocols and cannot be combined.
error.pairing_needs_capabilities: Connect both beds once before combining them so their motor layouts can be verified.
error.mismatched_motor_layouts: Those beds expose different motor layouts and cannot be combined safely.
error.octo_pairing_needs_connection: Both Octo beds must be connected before combining them so their capabilities can be saved.
error.pairing_unsupported_entities: One of these beds has controls that cannot be recreated safely while a paired side is offline, so pairing is blocked.

abort.not_enough_beds: Fewer than two active standalone beds remain, so this suggestion no longer applies.
abort.already_configured: These beds already belong to a paired Adjustable Bed entry.
abort.pairing_flow_failed: The Dual Bed setup flow could not be started. Reload Repairs and try again.
abort.beds_changed: The active standalone beds changed while this repair was open, so nothing was dismissed. Open the repair again to review the current set.
abort.beds_are_separate: Noted, the displayed beds are separate. The suggestion is gone and will not return while only those beds remain. If a new standalone bed is added, it may be suggested again.

octo_pin_required.title: PIN required for {name}
octo_pin_required.description:
**{name}** ({address}) is an Octo receiver whose PIN lock is engaged, and no PIN is configured in Home Assistant.

A locked receiver still connects and still reports its capabilities, but it will not act on commands until it is authenticated, so the controls appear to work while the bed does nothing.

**If you know the PIN:** open the OCTO Smart Control app (or your bed brand's version of it) to look it up, then enter it under **Settings → Devices & services → Adjustable Bed → Configure → Octo PIN**.

**If the PIN is lost:** there is no factory-default PIN. OCTO publishes a reset procedure per receiver at {recovery_url} — select yours by its photo. The two common ones are pressing the button on the controller *10 times in quick succession* (Receiver II / RC2, BrickMini Basic), or *once briefly then once long for about 10 seconds* (Brick 2 and others). Micro Lift receivers are reset from the remote instead.

⚠️ Every one of those is a full factory reset: all settings are irrevocably deleted and the remotes must be re-taught. A reset receiver has no PIN and is no longer locked.
